messages:
anya: Drafting a 'stagewise-cohort-prioritize' gate for new quant bring-ups. Idea: prioritize safety-sensitive cohorts (enterprises, high-usage slices) in the gating decision and allow faster rollback for them while letting low-risk cohorts continue in a degraded path.

matt: so different cohorts see different fallback behaviors? sounds useful. how do we define cohorts?

anya: cohort = (customer_tier OR traffic_slice). We'll compute a risk_score per cohort = exposure_weight * sensitivity_factor. High risk_score cohorts have stricter thresholds and immediate short-circuit to baseline on hard signals. Low risk_score cohorts use graduated fallback and soft-steer.

cal: propose mapping: enterprise=0.9, standard=0.5, canary-internal=0.2; slices like longdoc or paid-api get +0.2 sensitivity. Final risk_score clipped [0,1].

ops-bot: note: must emit `cohort_risk_score` and `effective_threshold` in telemetry for every decision to trace per-customer impact.

anya: gating rules sketch:
```
stagewise_cohort_prioritize:
  cohorts: [enterprise, standard, canary-internal]
  base_thresholds: {mrr:-0.02, fidelity:5%, p99:150}
  cohort_multipliers: {enterprise:0.6, standard:1.0, canary-internal:1.4}
  rule: breach if metric < base_threshold * multiplier_for_cohort
  hard_short_circuit: if hallucination_delta > 2% on any cohort -> immediate baseline for that cohort
  fallback_path_lowrisk: [int8_fallback, reduced_traffic, extended_shadow]
  fallback_path_highrisk: [immediate_baseline, notify_release_owner]
```

matt: small detail: multiplier <1 for enterprise means stricter threshold, right? good. Also add a per-cohort cool-down so we don't flip-flop for the same tenant.

anya: yep add `cooldown_minutes` default 120 per cohort. Also add `notify_channels` per cohort: enterprise -> #enterprise-notify and #eng-oncall, standard -> #eng-oncall only.

cal: simulation run: eval-bot run_id=84321 on v3q-staged:
```
samples=20k, cohort_split: enterprise 12%, standard 63%, canary-internal 25%
aggregate: mrr_delta: -0.015, fidelity_drop: 4.8%, p99:+10ms
per_cohort:
  enterprise: fidelity_drop=6.2% -> risk_score high -> breach threshold strict -> immediate baseline for enterprise cohort triggered
  standard: fidelity_drop=4.5% -> within cohort threshold -> enter fallback_path_lowrisk (int8_fallback + reduce to 5%)
  canary-internal: fidelity_drop=3.1% -> safe
decision: cohort-aware actions executed: route enterprise->baseline, standard->int8_fallback at 5%, canary-internal stays
```

anya: this is exactly the behavior we want: protect revenue and SLAs while still gathering signal from lower-risk cohorts.

matt: ops note: ensure rollout-controller logs the routing map so customer requests can be audited. Also add an API to opt a tenant into more aggressive testing if they opt-in.

eval-bot: follow-up after 40m: enterprise routed baseline -> no escalations; standard with int8_fallback saw fidelity improve to 3.9% drop and mrr_delta -0.009; canary-internal stable.

release-owner: I'll reach out to enterprise success to inform affected customers and include rollback rationale + remediation ETA. Do we want to auto-create a postmortem ticket when any cohort short-circuits?

anya: yes auto-create TKT and attach telemetry snapshot. Only auto-postmortem for hard short-circuits; soft cohort fallbacks should create a triage ticket but not full postmortem.

cal: one more thought: add a 'stale-signal dampener' to avoid reacting to transient spikes caused by upstream infra blips. Implement as a 10m min dwell or require two consecutive evaluation windows for low-risk cohorts. High-risk cohorts keep immediate reaction.

matt: agree. final action items: anya -> PR for gate + telemetry tags, cal -> add cohort routing audit logs, eval-bot -> add cohort split sim to smoke pipeline, release-owner -> prepare enterprise comms template.

ops-bot: runbook note created: "stagewise-cohort-prioritize" including config examples and playbook for enterprise notifications.

anya: thanks team. leaving thread open until PR merged and first live canary validates behavior.
